comparator.name: Public Administration
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted regulations prescribe 60 EC in each year for September 2026 entrants. Year three includes a 12 EC placement, a 12 EC thesis and 18 EC of approved minor or mobility study.
components: Introductory Seminar: Public Administration and Government
The first year also includes uncredited orientation and a Dutch language test.
Introduction to Public Sector Organisation Theory
This 6 EC course follows the 9 EC first-year research course.
Culture and Institutions in Public Administration
Complete at least 90 EC before starting this 12 EC placement. The placement lasts at least 40 working days and can involve professional or research work.
Complete at least 102 EC by the release of block 1 grades. The research proposal begins in block 2 and the thesis develops it through desk research in the second semester.
Choose 18 EC of minor study. The Examination Board must approve courses taken at an international university.

core: Public administration, government and the organisation of public institutions
Public policy formation, implementation and evaluation of societal problems
Politics, democratic governance and political decision-making
Constitutional and administrative law, rule of law and accountability
Public organisations, management and collaboration with civil society
Public finance and empirical public-administration research
adjacent: Local and regional governance and cross-sector cooperation
European governance and comparative public institutions
questions: How can governments design and evaluate responses to complex social problems?
How can public authority remain democratic, lawful and accountable?
How can public organisations collaborate and manage competing interests effectively?

alternatives.label: Public governance, policy & institutions
alternatives.labelReason: Public policy, political institutions, public economics and social research anchor the option, with comparative law and governance in support.
alternatives.concept: Study how governments design policies and how laws and institutions shape their decisions. Combine policy analysis, public economics and social research with comparative politics and law.
progression: Political and social inquiry supports public economics and policy analysis. Law, Society & Justice precedes public international law and comparative constitutional law.

alternatives.label: Public organisations, management & collaboration
alternatives.labelReason: Organisational behaviour and leadership combine with public policy, economics, civic institutions and communication.
alternatives.concept: Study how organisations make decisions, manage change and work with others on public problems. Combine leadership and communication with public policy, sustainability governance and social research.
alternatives.distinctness: This option focuses on people, leadership, negotiation and organisational change. The closest option gives more weight to public institutions and legal foundations.
progression: Comparative politics precedes Public Policy Analysis. Research methods and introductory leadership prepare for organisational psychology, negotiation and advanced social inquiry.

alternatives.label: Law, democracy & European governance
alternatives.labelReason: Comparative constitutional law, human rights, EU law and EU politics form a public-law and political institutions focus.
alternatives.concept: Study how laws and political institutions structure public authority. Compare constitutional systems, human rights and European governance, and investigate how they change over time.
alternatives.distinctness: Public law and European institutions anchor this option, with historical research and public economics. The other options emphasise policy analysis or organisational practice.
progression: Law, Society & Justice precedes international, constitutional and EU law. Comparative politics precedes European Union Politics.

blocks: Both compare legal traditions and institutions. Tilburg develops this topic in its public administration curriculum.
Both study political institutions and democracy. UCR emphasises comparison across political systems.
Both study European institutions and governance. UCR emphasises EU policymaking and political integration.
Both study public spending, taxation and economic choices. UCR emphasises market failure, efficiency and equity.
Both analyse how policy decisions are made and implemented. UCR uses a case study to examine the policy process.
Both study constitutional institutions and rights. UCR compares legal systems, while Tilburg introduces the Dutch framework.
Both introduce sociological theories and use them to study institutions and social life.
Both develop qualitative research design and methods such as interviewing and observation. Tilburg applies them to public administration.

selection.assessment: Three options address public policy and institutions, public organisations and collaboration, or comparative public law and European governance. Their different emphases are supported by their course selections.

notes.text: Tilburg combines public administration, law, policy and finance with a compulsory 12 EC placement and a 12 EC thesis. UCR offers related study across politics, law, organisations and research.
Tilburg teaches primarily in Dutch and offers some courses in English. UCR teaches in English.

audience.programmeDescription: Public Administration at Tilburg University studies how governments and public organisations make decisions and address social problems. Students combine policy, law and social research with a placement and thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related study in public policy and institutions, public organisations and collaboration, or law and European governance. Tilburg integrates these subjects in a dedicated public administration degree with a compulsory placement.
